_readme: Fingerprint of the schema that supabase/schema.sql + supabase/migrations/**
produce when replayed in the order declared by tests/schema-apply-order.json.
Regenerate ONLY with `node tests/schema-drift.mjs --write`, and only when the
schema change was intended — the diff of this file is the review surface.
What it can and cannot see is documented in the header of tests/schema-drift.mjs.

how: node tests/schema-drift.mjs --live-sql            -> read-only SQL, run it on production
node tests/schema-drift.mjs --live-compare r.json -> classify what came back
Level 1 sends nothing and returns a checksum per category plus one per table for
columns/constraints, so a clean surface costs ~180 short rows and names nothing.
Level 2 (--live-sql=<category>) returns the full name list for one category.
Both are pure SELECTs against the catalog. Production is never written.
result_2026_08_30: 7 of 9 categories are BYTE-IDENTICAL between production and a fresh replay of
this repo: relations (102), functions (261), policies (84), indexes (142),
triggers (18), rls (90), event_triggers (1). Identical hashes, not just counts.
That is the strongest statement this project has ever been able to make about
the repo matching the database, and it means NO whole object exists in
production and in no file, and NO object the chain builds is missing there.
columns and constraints each disagree on exactly ONE table; both are acknowledged
below. pg_cron was checked separately and OFF-fingerprint: 12 jobs, every one
scheduled by a migration in this repo, no orphans.

2026-08-30 later: hr_crops nullability FIXED on prod by 2026-09-03-crops-notnull-and-xp-prune-schedule.sql (columns now not null + defaults, matching the repo); acknowledgement retired in the same change.

acknowledged.what: a fresh replay builds TWO semantically identical checks — hr_bounty_monsters_hp_check (auto-named, from the inline  hp int not null default 1 check (hp >= 1)  in the create table) and hr_bounty_monsters_hp_chk (explicitly named) — where production has only hp_chk.
acknowledged.why: PATH-DEPENDENT, NOT A HAND-PATCH. 2026-08-23-bounty-monsters.generated.sql creates the table only  if to_regclass(...) is null . On production the table already existed from the pre-2026-08-30 revision of that generated file (which had no hp column at all), so the create-table branch was skipped and only the ADDITIVE  add column if not exists hp  +  add constraint hp_chk  ran. A fresh replay takes the create branch and gets both.
acknowledged.consequence: Cosmetic and permanent. Both databases enforce hp >= 1; the replay just enforces it twice under two names. The columns of this table match production exactly. Nothing to fix; recorded so a future reader does not mistake it for a missing migration and so --live-compare does not go red on it every run.

open: supabase_migrations.schema_migrations still holds 27 rows, the newest 2026-08-11; 12 of them have no file in this repo (anon_lockdown_public_default_fix, profiles_identity_authority_and_global_default_acl, profiles_drop_dead_update_policy, grant_hygiene_v2_detector, hr_rate_sample_weight_pin_search_path, player_tables_rls_initplan, cron_health_no_false_stale_on_new_jobs, maintenance_fn_revoke_service_role, revoke_hr_engine_from_authenticator, disarm_broken_market_crons, clan_leaderboard_join_policy, clan_join_policy_merge_r4_tolerance). RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-30: their effects are still fully reproduced — the object diff is clean in all 7 name-bearing categories — so no object is lost. Their SQL remains recoverable from that table s  statements  column. Nothing applied after 2026-08-11 is recorded there at all, because every later file was applied with execute_sql rather than apply_migration; that is why this checksum comparison, not the migrations table, is the source of truth for what production actually has.
NOT CHECKED HERE — grants and role memberships. hr_assert_grant_hygiene() owns that surface (cron  hr-grant-hygiene , 04:50 daily) and is a stronger check than a fingerprint. Do not duplicate it.

NOT CHECKED SYSTEMATICALLY — function BODIES. The fingerprint carries signatures only; all 261 match by signature, which does NOT mean the bodies match. Spot-checked 3 on 2026-08-30: hr_rpc_gate and hr_cron_health are md5-IDENTICAL to the replay (the hr_rpc_gate hotfix restore was folded back into the repo correctly); hr_apply differs by 138 chars, which is exactly one two-line comment present in the file and absent from the deployed body — code identical, behaviour identical. The header note this replaces claimed hr_apply was a stale 25,966-char revision against a 40,754-char file; both numbers were three revisions out of date. See blind spot (C).
NOT CHECKED — whether any row survives a restore. As of 2026-08-30 no restore test has ever been run against this project. See blind spot (B).
